approach:
Add one reading check, `check_outcome_state(reading, request)`, to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs as a `step!` line right after `check_governance_coverage`. It skips a reading with no capability, a question, no deliverables, or no detected delivery. It fires only when a delivery verb (publish, deploy, share, release) is used as a verb at a verb position AND has an audience-visible object. It is satisfied only by (a) a criterion of kind BEHAVIOR that has a whole-word state phrase (reachable, is served, http 200, downloadable and similar), or (b) an out_of_scope item that names every detected verb or its -ing form as a whole word. A content criterion that holds a state phrase does not satisfy it (answers finding 1). Technical nouns (crate, package, binary, image, app, artifact) count as objects only with a destination word or a version token in the window (finding 2). The replay test is table-driven: the measured count covers only entries whose text is verbatim, the stand-in entries are a labelled scope illustration, and the CHANGELOG assertions follow the table (finding 3). D161 avoids the phrases the decision-log parse reads as supersession (finding 4). The claim stays: the check covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs (20261014-082328-g6vy); 20261014-174815-7bf8 and 20261017-173508-0wtc are another class, not caught, and their recorded requests are not replayed unless the host supplies them. The 5% is an estimate.

Verb positions: a verb counts at a segment start, after a list marker (`2)`, `(a)`, `1.`, `-`, `*`), or after a lead-in (`and`, `then`, `please`, `also`, `should`, `can you`, `could you`, `would you`, `want to`, `need to`, `like to`, `going to`). A segment starts at the first word, after a newline, or after `.!?:;` followed by white space or the end, so `crates.io` and `v1.2` do not break one. I read the code to settle the kind question: `check_code_survey` (reading.rs 3559) fires only for class_of_work `code` or `tests`; `governed_reading` builds class `feature` (scoped_reading, line 6180) and the corpus `base_reading` builds class `docs` (refusal_corpus.rs line 131), so a Behavior state criterion on those fixtures triggers no survey. `check_criteria_evidence` (line 3451) reads only producer-report phrases, so the new criteria avoid those.

decisions.choice: Put the check in reading acceptance as `step!(check_outcome_state(reading, request))` right after `check_governance_coverage` and before `check_boundary_and_repo_files`.
decisions.reason: The fault starts where a reading is accepted: a delivery verb read as a narrow deliverable, with no check against the state the user observes. The governance refusal for a publish request names the missing workflow and is the more specific repair, so it stays first. The new check reads only the reading's criteria, out_of_scope and request (like the governance check), so it sits before the file-comparison checks. The corpus case `delivery-request-naming-a-workflow-fails-governance-first` pins the order.

rejected.option: Change the reader prompt or READING_RULES
rejected.why: Out of scope. Reader budget is 1997 of 2000 and the briefs test fixes 6 rules. The refusal text reaches the reader on the re-read.

rejected.option: Put the check first, or in the verifier
rejected.why: First would hide the governance refusal that names the workflow. The verifier sees the problem only after the producer has run.

rejected.option: A general glossary or figurative-term check

decisions.choice: The state phrase must be in a criterion of kind Behavior. A Content criterion with a state phrase does not satisfy the check. The error says to add a behavior criterion.
decisions.reason: Finding 1. A content criterion can be met by a Grep on a file, so 'docs/explainer.md says the page is reachable' still checks only that a file exists, the g6vy misread in disguise. Behavior-evidence asks for criteria that check the behavior happening. Requiring kind AND phrase is strictly tighter than the phrase alone. check_code_survey does not fire on the test fixtures (class feature or docs); for a real code-class delivery reading it would also ask for a survey, which is correct for such a reading.

rejected.option: Accept a state phrase in any criterion kind
rejected.why: Lets a file-only content criterion pass by wording; the earlier plan's reason for rejecting the kind rule was a non sequitur.

rejected.option: Check the criterion kind alone, with no phrase list
rejected.why: A behavior criterion such as 'docs/x.md exists' would pass; the phrase names the observable state.

decisions.choice: Fire only for an audience-visible object within 5 words of the verb in the same segment (stopping at before/after/when/while/if/because/until/unless). VISIBLE nouns: page(s), site, website, docs, documentation, explainer, guide, book, report, tutorial, article, dashboard. A `v<digits>` token, a destination word (npm, pypi, docker, crates.io, registry, production, online, pages) or an audience word (team, everyone, colleagues, customers, stakeholders, readers, public) also counts. PACKAGE nouns (crate, crates, package, binary, app, image, artifact) count only when a destination word or a version token is also in the window. A pronoun object (it, them, these, those) counts only if such a word appears earlier in the segment. A first following word in NOUN_FOLLOWERS (notes, note, process, pipeline, workflow, checklist, candidate, date, plan, button, of) makes it a noun use.
decisions.reason: Finding 2 and the precedent in check_governance_coverage's doc (reading.rs about lines 3308-3310): a word table that refused ordinary requests was removed. In a Rust workspace crate, package, image and binary are technical nouns, so 'Share the parsing code between crates', 'Workers should share the package cache' and 'Release the image buffer before returning' must not match. Corpus accepting cases pin them. The remaining false refusal ('Release the page lock') is stated as a limit.

rejected.option: Keep crate, package, binary, image, app, artifact as plain object words
Fire on any verb at a verb position
rejected.why: Technical verb senses (release a lock, share a client, publish an event) are the larger group; asking for a reachable URL there wastes the single re-read.

rejected.option: Detect the verb in any position or by substring
rejected.why: Refuses 'a share button', 'the release process', 'shared helpers'.

decisions.choice: List markers and sentence breaks are handled explicitly by a private tokenizer: a segment-start word that is all digits or one ASCII letter, followed by `)` or `.` and white space, passes the segment start to the next word. `-`, `*` and `1.` are covered by the newline rule.
decisions.reason: The input forms must be handled: dash and star bullets, `1.` / `2)` / `(a)` parts, a newline after 'Priority: high'. A dot inside `crates.io` or `v1.2` does not break a segment.

rejected.option: Segment start only after a newline or .!?:;
rejected.why: Misses `2) Deploy the site` and `(a) Release v1`.

decisions.choice: The state-phrase list is whole-word lowercase phrases checked with has_phrase on a normalized criterion: reachable, is served, are served, served at, served from, served page, http 200, 200 ok, is live, goes live, live at, available at https, available at http, accessible at https, opens in a browser, loads in a browser, can be downloaded, can download, available for download, downloadable, installable, can be installed from. Left out: url, tag, link, page, can open, can be opened, serves, bare available at.
decisions.reason: Those left-out words occur in file-only criteria ('the <title> tag names the page', 'A reader can open docs/explainer.md', 'docs/explainer.md is available at docs/'). Tests refuse them even as behavior criteria, which proves the phrase list and not the kind does that work. `reachable` alone is a known limit.

rejected.option: Keep url, tag, can open and bare available at

decisions.choice: The out_of_scope exit needs the verb or its -ing form as a whole word in an item, not followed by a NOUN_FOLLOWERS word; with several verbs each must be covered, unless a behavior criterion names a state. It does not reuse `governance_is_covered` (substring `contains`).
decisions.reason: A substring match lets 'Changes to shared helpers' and 'Release notes are unchanged' satisfy the exit (earlier finding c).

decisions.choice: Claim only what is shown. The CHANGELOG, doc comment and D161 say the check covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs (g6vy) and that the request texts of 7bf8 and 0wtc are not replayed (stand-in text only) unless the host supplies them. The replay test is table-driven with a `verbatim: bool` per entry. The measured assertion runs only over verbatim entries (caught verbatim count; refuse g6vy). The stand-in entries are asserted not refused in a separate, labelled illustration block whose comment says it is not a measurement and cannot fail on the recorded text. The CHANGELOG assertions use counts computed from the table: `covers {caught} of the {total} cited jobs` and `replayed for {verbatim} of the {total}`; the 'not replayed' phrase is required exactly while verbatim < total. Nothing asserts a fixed 'one verbatim'.
decisions.reason: Finding 3. The snapshot lacks records/ (only paraphrases of 7bf8 and 0wtc exist in docs/decisions.md), so text written by the planner without delivery verbs cannot fail. Computing the measured count over verbatim entries only keeps the claim honest, and following the table keeps the test valid if the host supplies the texts and the entries flip to verbatim.

rejected.option: Present stand-ins as the recorded requests
rejected.why: Not true; the evidence default forbids it.

rejected.option: Assert 'exactly one verbatim' as a constant
rejected.why: Contradicts the fallback where the host supplies the texts.

rejected.option: Claim the whole class, or 3 of 3
rejected.why: Findings a and b of job 20261027-054230-8nz8.

decisions.choice: The 5% stays an estimate. The doc comment and CHANGELOG say 'expected 5% of newly refused readings' and label it a guess. D161 records that the check has no reader rule (reader budget 1997 of 2000, READING_RULES fixed at 6) and costs one re-read. D161 never uses 'supersedes', 'superseded by' or 'amends' and does not name D08 or other entries.
decisions.reason: Nothing measured the rate. Finding 4: the decision-log parse (crates/athena-cli/src/backtest.rs PHRASES, line 78) reads those three phrases and each hit needs a [[link]] in docs/decision-links.toml, which is not a deliverable. The governed-path link for D08 is not triggered because reading.rs is not a governed path.

Add a private tokenizer: lowercase, curly apostrophes made straight, words as runs of alphanumeric characters (and `'`) with byte ranges. A word is segment-start when it is first, when the gap before it holds a newline, or when the gap holds one of `.!?:;` followed by white space or the end of the gap. Then the list-marker rule: a segment-start word that is all digits or one ASCII letter, with the gap after it trimmed equal to `)` or `.`, makes the next word segment-start too. Add `delivery_verbs(request) -> Vec<(&'static str, &'static str)>` (verb, -ing form, deduplicated). A verb counts when it is segment-start, or the previous word is a single lead-in, or the previous two words are a lead-in pair; and its first following word is not in NOUN_FOLLOWERS; and within the next 5 words of the same segment (stopping at a STOP_WORDS word) there is a VISIBLE_NOUN, a `v<digits>` token, a DESTINATION_WORD or an AUDIENCE_WORD, or a PACKAGE_NOUN together with a DESTINATION_WORD or a version token; or one of the next 2 words is a pronoun and such a word appears earlier in the same segment. Add `out_of_scope_names(item, verb, ing)`: the verb or -ing form as a whole word not followed by a NOUN_FOLLOWERS word. Normalize each criterion (lowercase, collapse white space) and test it with `has_phrase`.

Add `pub fn check_outcome_state(reading: &Reading, request: &str) -> Result<()>`. Return Ok when capability is none, a question is set, deliverables are empty, or `delivery_verbs` is empty. Return Ok when any criterion of kind `CriterionKind::Behavior` has a state phrase, or when every detected verb is covered by an out_of_scope item (unless a behavior state criterion exists). Otherwise `bail!` with one line starting 'the reading was refused because', naming each verb, saying that no behavior criterion names a state the audience can observe (a content criterion that mentions a state still only checks a file), and giving the repairs: a behavior criterion with a reachable URL, a served page or a downloadable release, or an out_of_scope item that names the delivery (for example 'Publishing is out of scope'). The error must contain `reachable URL`, `served page` and the lowercase verb. The doc comment is one `///` paragraph block with no blank `///` line. It names the root cause (a delivery verb read as a narrow deliverable, with no check against the state the user observes), says the check covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs (20261014-082328-g6vy), names 20261014-174815-7bf8 (ladder of requirements) and 20261017-173508-0wtc (ontology decision) as outside the check and not replayed, lists verbs, positions, object rule, behavior-kind rule and limits, and states 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.' and that the 5% is an estimate, not a measurement.

risks.risk: False refusals: a technical use with a visible object word (for example 'Release the page lock') is refused.
risks.mitigation: The visible-object rule keeps technical verb uses unmatched and package nouns need a destination or version token. Corpus accept cases pin 'Release the lock before awaiting', 'Workers should share the HTTP client', 'Publish the event to the bus', 'Share the parsing code between crates' and 'Release the image buffer before returning'. The error says exactly what to add, and D161 states the page-lock limit. The verification-time replay holds the job if the real refusal rate is above 10%.

risks.risk: False negatives: other verbs (ship, launch, post, upload), gerund starts, verbs in comma lists, unlisted objects, and a behavior criterion that says only `reachable` of a file.
risks.mitigation: The claim is limited to four verbs, the listed positions and object words. The doc comment, CHANGELOG and D161 say so.

risks.risk: The stand-in texts for 7bf8 and 0wtc could be read as proof that the check does not fire on the recorded requests.
risks.mitigation: Stand-ins are labelled in the fixture, test comment, CHANGELOG, D161 and doc comment. The measured block covers verbatim entries only, and the CHANGELOG assertion requires 'not replayed' while any entry is not verbatim.

risks.risk: The replay test cannot be settled because the recorded texts of two jobs are absent from the snapshot.
risks.mitigation: The test follows the table, so supplying the texts only flips two flags. Two open questions ask the host for the texts and the user whether the scope-only reading of criterion 2 is accepted.

risks.risk: Another existing test with a delivery request and a file-only reading breaks and is missed.
risks.mitigation: Step 5 lists the three reading.rs tests and step 6 the corpus case found by grep. Step 10 greps all of crates/ and runs `cargo test`; a failure is fixed by adding a Behavior state criterion.

risks.risk: Requiring the Behavior kind makes a code-class delivery reading also need a `Code survey:` assumption (check_code_survey).
risks.mitigation: That is the existing rule for code readings with behavior criteria and not a new refusal reason; the fixtures use classes feature and docs. D161 notes it.

risks.risk: New text trips the boundary scan, the personal-data allow-list or the decision-log parse.
risks.mitigation: The producer avoids the boundary words and email-like text, and writes D161 without 'supersedes', 'superseded by' or 'amends' and without naming another decision. `cargo test` runs the policy and decisions tests.

risks.risk: Tokenizer edge cases move a segment boundary (list marker, dotted name).
risks.mitigation: The detection test table covers `-`, `*`, `1.`, `2)`, `(a)`, a newline after 'Priority: high', `crates.io` and `v1.2`. Corpus bullet counts pin `N)` and `(a)` parts at 0 bullets as at existing cases (lines 288 to 313).

risks.risk: CHANGELOG line wrapping breaks the phrase assertions.
risks.mitigation: The assertions collapse white space first, as the existing CHANGELOG assertion does (refusal_corpus.rs line 859).

risks.mitigation: The refusal text states what to add. D161 records the cost (one re-read) and that a reader rule needs a budget decision outside this job.

demonstrations.method: Unit test `check_outcome_state_refuses_the_g6vy_misread` in `mod tests` of reading.rs. It builds `governed_reading(&["docs/explainer.md"], &["docs/explainer.md exists"], &[])` (Content criterion, class feature) and calls `check_outcome_state`, `check_reading_acceptance` and `refusing_check` with the request 'Publish a first explainer page on how firstmate handles work.' Each must refuse; the error must contain `reachable URL`, `served page` and `publish`; `refusing_check` must return the name `check_outcome_state`.
demonstrations.observes: The g6vy request with a file-only criterion is refused by check_outcome_state, and the error names a reachable URL and a served page. 'page' is the 4th word after 'Publish', inside the 5-word window.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without `check_outcome_state` in `refusing_check`, `refusing_check` returns None and `check_reading_acceptance` returns Ok, so the unwrap_err and name assertions fail; without the function the test does not compile.

Fixture: the plain `Reading` from `governed_reading` (exists, line 7013, over `scoped_reading` at 6157), passed as an argument; no double. Test added by step 5.

demonstrations.method: Test `delivery_verb_replay_over_the_cited_jobs` in refusal_corpus.rs. A table of three entries (job, request, `verbatim: bool`, source label): g6vy with the request as quoted in the brief, verbatim true; 7bf8 and 0wtc as stand-in text built from D94 and D152, verbatim false, labelled 'stand-in, not the recorded request'. For each it builds `base_reading(request)`, runs `refusing_check(.., Some(&repo_files()))` and records whether the first refusal is `check_outcome_state`. Measured block: over verbatim entries only, asserts g6vy is refused and computes `caught` from the table. Illustration block (separate comment: scope, not a measurement): the stand-ins are not refused, so the whole caught set is {g6vy} and caught is 1 of total 3. CHANGELOG (via include_str!, white space collapsed) must contain `format!("covers {caught} of the {total} cited jobs")` and `format!("replayed for {verbatim} of the {total}")`, and 'not replayed' exactly while verbatim < total. If the host supplies the texts the entries flip to verbatim and the same test still holds.
demonstrations.observes: g6vy is refused by check_outcome_state; the two stand-ins are accepted; the caught count is 1 and the total is 3; the CHANGELOG states the same count and says which requests were replayed.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check the caught set is empty and the g6vy assertion fails. A CHANGELOG count that differs from the table, or a missing 'not replayed' while a stand-in remains, fails the phrase assertions.

CHANGELOG read with `include_str!` as at refusal_corpus.rs line 859. Test added by step 7. The stand-in half cannot fail on the recorded text and says so in its comment.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in reading.rs. (1) `check_outcome_state_accepts_a_behavior_state_for_each_delivery_verb`, through `check_reading_acceptance`, with a Behavior criterion added by a test helper: 'Publish the explainer page' / 'The page is reachable at its public URL'; 'Deploy the site on every push' / 'The site is served at the deployed address'; 'Share the report with the team' / 'The shared link is reachable by the recipient'; 'Release v1' / 'The v1 release assets are downloadable'. Each is accepted. The same requests with only 'docs/x.md exists' are refused, and with the content criterion 'docs/explainer.md says the page is reachable' are refused, while the same text as a Behavior criterion is accepted. 'Add a timeout setting' with a file-only criterion is accepted. (2) `delivery_verbs_are_found_after_lead_ins_and_markers` calls the private `delivery_verbs` on 'Build the docs and publish them', 'Can you deploy the site', 'I want to release v1', '* Publish the page', '- Publish the page', '1. Share the report', '2) Deploy the site', '(a) Release v1' and 'Priority: high\n\nPublish the page' and asserts the verb is found; it asserts none is found in 'Add release notes', 'Add a share button', 'Rename shared helpers', 'Add tests for share and release.', 'We deployed it', 'Add a timeout setting', 'Release the lock before awaiting', 'Workers should share the HTTP client', 'Publish the event to the bus', 'Share the parsing code between crates', 'Workers should share the package cache', 'Release the image buffer before returning' and 'and release the slot on failure'; and finds one in 'Publish the crate to crates.io' and 'Release the binary as v1'. (3) Corpus cases `delivery-verb-after-and`, `delivery-verb-after-can-you`, `delivery-verb-after-want-to` (Refuse), `delivery-state-in-a-content-criterion-refused` (Refuse) and `delivery-verb-technical-use-is-accepted` (Accept) run the same shapes through `refusing_check`.
demonstrations.observes: A Behavior criterion with a state phrase is accepted for publish, deploy, share and release; a file-only or content-kind state criterion is refused for each; detection works at every listed position, fails on noun uses and on technical uses with no visible object; 'Add a timeout setting' is not refused.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without lead-in detection the three lead-in requests are not found, so the unit test and the Refuse corpus cases fail. Without the state list the accepting pairs are refused. Without the object rule and the package-noun rule the technical-use accept cases are refused. Without the kind rule the content-kind state criterion is accepted.

demonstrations.method: Unit test `out_of_scope_and_incidental_words_do_not_satisfy_the_check`. A Share request ('Share the report with the team') with out_of_scope ['Changes to shared helpers'] is refused; a Release request ('Release v1') with ['Release notes are unchanged'] is refused; the same requests with ['Sharing the report is out of scope'] and ['Releasing is out of scope: no tag is cut'] are accepted. A publish request ('Publish the explainer page') is refused when the only extra criterion, of kind Behavior, is each of 'the <title> tag names the page', 'The URL field is documented', 'A reader can open docs/explainer.md' and 'docs/explainer.md is available at docs/'. Corpus cases `delivery-verb-out-of-scope-shared-helpers-refused`, `delivery-verb-out-of-scope-release-notes-refused` (Refuse) and `delivery-verb-out-of-scope-names-it-accepted` (Accept) run the same shapes through `refusing_check`.
demonstrations.observes: Substring and incidental words (shared, Release notes, tag, URL, can open, available at) do not satisfy the check, even in a behavior criterion; a whole-word verb or -ing form in out_of_scope does.
demonstrations.fails_without: A substring match on out_of_scope accepts 'Changes to shared helpers' and 'Release notes are unchanged', so the Refuse assertions fail. A state list that holds tag, url, can open or bare available at accepts the refused criteria.
